dear @jackfriks & @marclou,

you probably don't know me, we certainly never met, but i wanted to write this to express how disappointing this whole hackathon thing has been

first of all, you are working together with a company whose nickname in the industry is literally scamfield (thanks to their dark patterns, targeting children in their marketing, promising fake unlimited usage, etc etc)

you two have more than 500k followers just on X alone & tons of sway among the developer crowd - why not use it to partner with other, more builder-native companies like cursor or replit?

but ok, these companies probably have some dirt on them as well, but unfortunately this isn't all

secondly, the fact you charged $99 to enter a hackathon - which are normally free - felt extremely predatory

and the fact that you instantly backtracked showed that you ultimately came to the same conclusion

but ok, we all make mistakes and learn from them, shit happens

however, and thirdly, as other pointed out: hackathons aren't a thing you just do on the side - there are literal businesses build around organizing & doing them well

and the lack of organization really is showing at the moment

not only the fact that the prize pool is unevenly distributed but more so that you didn't seem to have bothered with setting up proper guard rails

which now led to @indexsy, an internet OG who has been in the game for a decade+, who himself has a six figure following across socials, and makes multiple millions per year, enter the contest - and wipe the floor with all of the other participants

it's become so much of a farce that jacky is even making fun of indie hackers - the very same audience you are trying to inspire

which now puts you in a kobayashi maru - damned if you kick him out, damned if you don't

now, all of this would maybe be somewhat understandable if you guys were starving creators who have a tough time monetizing their audience

but you quite literally don't need any of this bullshit given that you guys generate, what, $150k per month between the two of you??!!

if i'm being very blunt - and i want to emphasize i have no insight knowledge on this - it feels like you were simply paid by higgsfield to run this contest as a marketing stunt for them 

(i sincerely hope i'm wrong and please feel free to call me out on this if it isn't the case)

ultimately, the reason why i (and many others i assume) follow you guys is because you build dope shit & have tons of fun along the way

would love to see more of that & less of whatever this whole situation turned out to be...

candidates.text:
here is a pro tip for those of you that are trying to be better story tellers. & it's completely free.

you see most ppl create stories in isolation. this is a mistake. cuz you are treating every thing as a standalone entity if you will. 

everything you create should be in service of a singular larger unfolding narrative.

e.g. a post from a year ago is not dead, it's just chapter 43 in a larger context. it's a story you can revisit, build upon, challenge, or extend in a meaningful way.

this is what makes story telling platforms so powerful. imagine you're assigned a potentially large task, what do you do? well you break it into smaller parts, & then build the large part up over time. it's the same principle here. this also works in interviews or any other setting.

your entire existence should be one unfolding narrative. this is also true for marketing & brands. most if not all of the chief communications officers miss this as well (even though they get paid c suite dollars & you're a lowbie). most important rule is that you should think macro, execute micro.

some ppl might read it & find this to be obvious (& it's usually the very IQ ppl who think they know everything) but there are like maybe a handful of ppl that actually execute on this well on the planet.

candidates.text:
it's very strange that i prefer listening to pods on youtube over any other platform (& so does everyone else).

even though most of the time i am not watching the video at all, it's in the background. but just knowing it's there is psychologically powerful. i can glance over & see the ppl talking, expressions, etc. this makes the experience so much better.

if you told someone a decade ago that youtube would become the largest podcasting platform they'd think you were kinda nuts. i mean why would anyone want to *watch* a podcast?

it turns out humans really enjoy looking at other humans. even if they aren't really doing anything other than talking. the facial expressions, the sets, are all important. 

so podcasts were basically just new talk shows masquerading as an audio only format all along. which is why netflix is finally going ham on pods exclusively.
